correctness.rationale: For every integer \(n\ge2\), the exact current deposition rate is \(m^2-k\), the three edge-class counts sum to this rate, and first-event conditioning proves the rational Laplace recurrence. The normalized overlap drift and second-factorial-moment control yield \(\mathbb E[(K_m)_2]\le C m^2(m-1)^2/[n(n-1)]\), with \(C<3\). The telescoping time-reward identity then gives \(\left|\mathbb E[T_n]-H_n^{(2)}+1/n\right|\le C[6(H_{n+1}-3/2)+\pi^2/6]/[n(n-1)]\). The asymptotic follows analytically. Independent labeled-mask rational recursion checks means and two distinct Laplace values for \(2\le n\le7\), without replacing the proof. No generalization to changing rates or stochastic order is claimed.

originality.rationale: The new statement is a sharp \(-1/n\) mean-time correction and complete rational Laplace transform for the last accepted event under unit-rate edge adsorption on a complete bipartite graph with one forbidden perfect matching. Known random greedy matching results principally concern final matching sizes; a last-event clock additionally depends on the full path of state-dependent holding rates and overlap correlations. The closest earlier claim for the same graph establishes terminal matching-size deficiency and explicitly excludes time-resolved kinetics. Examined primary literature did not imply this clock law. Historical priority remains provisional because older full texts were not universally accessible.

value.rationale: The time of the last successful deposition is a standard kinetic observable distinct from final jammed matching size. The complete transform and signed \(-1/n\) mean-time correction show that removing a perfect matching of adsorption edges can accelerate expected completion asymptotically despite reducing instantaneous attempt rates. A rigorous explicit error bound makes the result a natural infinite-family benchmark and not merely a small-size computation. No general downstream theorem is claimed.
